solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: One musician has claimed nothing working — for another? (10)

indicatorNotes.has claimed: to claim is to take hold of, so the player holds the letters inside

blocks.note: a bass player, the first musician

annotation.surface: A musician has been hired for nothing, filling in for a colleague.
annotation.walkthrough: One musician looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay; 'another' with its question mark is the definition, the player the bassist turns into.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a bassoonist is a different musician from the bassist, hence 'another', the question mark flagging how vague that is.

entries.clue: Dwarf heard bee in tree (4)

indicatorNotes.heard: we only hear the insect's name, which is the sound of the letter B
indicatorNotes.in: the B goes inside the tree

blocks.note: the letter B is said like the insect

annotation.surface: A tiny figure hears a bee buzzing in a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: Dwarf is an adjective here, meaning miniature, as in baby carrots or a baby grand.
annotation.definitionFit: Baby as an adjective means much smaller than usual, which is what dwarf means of plants.

entries.clue: Splash of drink, aerated originally? (4)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of Splash, Of, Drink and Aerated

annotation.surface: A dash of something fizzy added to a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: its initials spell the answer, and read plainly it describes soda water topping up a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Soda water is aerated, and a splash of it is added to drinks like whisky.

entries.clue: Viewing article in newspaper, girls beyond hope missing leader (5,7)

indicatorNotes.beyond: the newspaper and girls come after OPE

blocks.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper

annotation.surface: Someone reading about girls in a newspaper story who are past all hope.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as if an article appears in the paper, but article is part of the definition: an item, a thing used for viewing.
annotation.definitionFit: Opera glasses are small binoculars, an article for viewing the stage.

entries.clue: Broadcast originally called The Sound of Hackney? (5)

indicatorNotes.Broadcast: put out on air, so heard rather than seen

blocks.note: née, placed before a maiden name, means originally called, and is said nay

annotation.surface: A radio or TV programme titled The Sound of Hackney, the London borough.
annotation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London district, but a hackney is a breed of horse, so its sound is a neigh.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-style sense: hackney is a breed of riding horse as well as a London borough, and the cry of any horse is its whinny.

entries.clue: Cut, with hole punctured, concerned with what may be required? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.punctured: the cut goes right through the middle of the hole

blocks.note: a sty is a filthy hole, a pigsty

annotation.surface: A tyre is cut and punctured, and the driver thinks about what is needed.
annotation.walkthrough: The talk of a hole and a puncture sets the scene: after a flat, the spare tyre is what may be required.
annotation.definitionFit: When a tyre is punctured, a spare tyre may be needed to carry on.

entries.clue: Measure in square feet, one about third of yard (4)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so ACE is wrapped around the letter
indicatorNotes.third of: third of picks out the letter standing in third place in the word that follows

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

annotation.surface: Someone measures an area in square feet, a yard at a time.
annotation.walkthrough: An acre is 43,560 square feet, so it can be expressed in square feet.
annotation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of area, measurable in square feet.

entries.clue: Living wonderful with an amphipod, say (10)

blocks.note: to earn a crust is to make a living

annotation.surface: A cheerful remark about life being grand alongside a small sea creature.
annotation.walkthrough: Living reads as an adjective but is the noun: a crust, as in earning a crust, is a livelihood.
annotation.definitionFit: Amphipods, such as sandhoppers, are small crustaceans; say marks the example.

entries.clue: Board to apply leverage to business (10)

blocks.note: to board a ship or train is to enter it
to prise is to force open with a lever

annotation.surface: Advice to a company board to use its leverage on the business.
annotation.walkthrough: Board looks like the company directors; it is the verb, to get on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an enterprise is a business venture or company, the word used in 'free enterprise'.

entries.clue: Bird in capital city on move, heading for resort (10)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, RIGA going on the move sits after it

blocks.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

annotation.surface: A bird in a capital city takes off for a holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: On the move looks like one phrase meaning travelling; it splits so that on places the city after BUDGE.
annotation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small Australian parrot, a popular cage bird.

entries.clue: Work of art destroyed (4)

blocks.note: a sculpture of head and shoulders

annotation.surface: A work of art has been wrecked.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are everyday: a sculpted head and shoulders, and the slang for broken.
annotation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpture, a work of art; bust also means broken or destroyed.

entries.clue: Girl with tandem, in travelling, providing a trip (4-8)

indicatorNotes.travelling: something travelling is on the move and does not stay put, so the letters shift position

annotation.surface: A girl on a tandem bicycle, out travelling, going on an excursion.
annotation.walkthrough: Trip looks like a journey, fitting the tandem; it is the drug experience.
annotation.definitionFit: A mind-altering drug produces a trip, a hallucinatory experience.

entries.clue: Till search, tigers roaming free? (4,8)

indicatorNotes.roaming free: the letters wander loose and rearrange

annotation.surface: Keep hunting until the tigers are running wild.
annotation.walkthrough: Till reads as the word meaning until; it is the shop's money drawer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: till is the everyday word for the shop machine that records sales and holds the takings.

entries.clue: Dressing in bag bandaging boy, great quantity (5,5)

indicatorNotes.bandaging: the bag wraps round the boy like a bandage

blocks.note: a sac is a bag or pouch

annotation.surface: A boy's wound is wrapped with a big supply of dressing from a bag.
annotation.walkthrough: Dressing and bandaging paint a first-aid scene; the dressing is for a salad. Salad cream is a British bottled mayonnaise-like condiment.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this British bottled condiment is one kind of dressing for salads.

entries.clue: Stars get it wrong in general? (10)

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Celebrities generally get things wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: In general reads as a phrase meaning usually; general is the army officer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the army officer: a general's craft is planning campaigns, which is strategy.

entries.clue: Weapons hardly found aboard vessel (9)

indicatorNotes.found aboard: ILL is carried inside the vessel

blocks.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill = hardly, as in 'can ill afford'

annotation.surface: Almost no weapons are found on board a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: Vessel looks like a ship, fitting aboard; it is a blood vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Artillery is heavy guns, weapons collectively.

entries.clue: Furniture item, extremely sturdy in every aspect (4,5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extreme letters of sturdy
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the two letters are placed within the word for every

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Sturdy
an air is a look or aspect

annotation.surface: A piece of furniture advertised as solid in every respect.
annotation.walkthrough: Extremely sturdy sounds like strong praise, but extremely just asks for the two end letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a large upholstered armchair for relaxing is one item of furniture.

entries.clue: Colour scheme in gold introduced by Jan’s predecessor (5)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: the month comes first and leads in the gold

blocks.note: December comes before January; DEC is the calendar abbreviation

annotation.surface: A gold colour scheme brought in by the person who held Jan's job before her.
annotation.walkthrough: Jan looks like a person with a predecessor in a job; it is the month January.
annotation.definitionFit: Decor is the decoration and furnishing of a room, including its colour scheme.

entries.clue: Iraqis, say, fixing braking system on vehicle losing its front end (5)

indicatorNotes.losing its front end: the car drops its first letter
indicatorNotes.on: the braking system is attached to the vehicle, after it

annotation.surface: Iraqi mechanics repair the brakes on a car whose front has been smashed.
annotation.walkthrough: Front end sounds like the bumper; here it is just the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Iraq is an Arab country, so its people are one instance of the wider group, which say signals.

entries.clue: A bomb dropped with charges (9)

blocks.note: to shed is to drop, as leaves
a charge is a load, as a charge of powder

annotation.surface: A bomb is released along with explosive charges.
annotation.walkthrough: A bomb is British slang for a lot of money, as in costs a bomb; shedloads also means a huge amount.
annotation.definitionFit: Both a bomb and shedloads are informal for a very large amount, especially of money.

entries.clue: Axes removing articles, too sharp? (6-6)

indicatorNotes.removing: the axes lose their articles, each A

blocks.note: two cleavers, axes for chopping meat
A, the indefinite article, once from each cleaver

annotation.surface: Axes are said to be too sharp once the items are taken away.
annotation.walkthrough: Axes is plural, so two cleavers; each loses its A to leave CLEVER twice.
annotation.definitionFit: Clever-clever means showing off one's cleverness, too sharp for one's own good.

entries.clue: Be safe initially during flight (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of safe is used
indicatorNotes.during: the S sits inside the flight

annotation.surface: Advice to stay safe while on a plane.
annotation.walkthrough: Flight looks like air travel; it is fleeing, an exit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be, in the sense of 'to be or not to be', is simply to have being in the world.

entries.clue: Sporting festival (4)

blocks.note: sporting = playing by the rules, just, as in a sporting chance
a festival with stalls and rides, a fete

annotation.surface: A sports festival.
annotation.walkthrough: Sporting reads as athletic, but it means fair-minded, as in a sporting gesture.
annotation.definitionFit: Sporting means fair and generous; a fair is also a festival.

entries.clue: Captain underwater, sign surfacing? (4)

indicatorNotes.surfacing: in a down answer, coming up means written upwards, so turned round

annotation.surface: A submarine captain watches for a sign he should come up.
annotation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: Jules Verne's submarine commander is the most famous captain who works beneath the sea.

entries.clue: Release when healer pulled back? (4)

indicatorNotes.pulled back: drawn backwards, so read right to left

blocks.note: time is the great healer, as the saying goes

annotation.surface: A patient is discharged once the doctor withdraws.
annotation.walkthrough: Healer suggests a doctor, but the proverb says time is a healer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to release gas, light or sound is to send it out, as a chimney does smoke.

entries.clue: Open door for kisser, one glowing at being let in (10)

indicatorNotes.being let in: the three pieces are admitted inside the kisser

blocks.note: kisser is slang for the mouth or face

annotation.surface: Someone opens the door for a kiss, glowing at being let in.
annotation.walkthrough: Kisser looks like a person who kisses; it is slang for the face.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to open the door for something is to make it easier or possible, which is the verb's meaning.

entries.clue: Some sum at Harvard? (4)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the following words is taken

annotation.surface: An arithmetic problem set at an American university.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: Americans say math where the British say maths, so a sum at Harvard is math.
annotation.definitionFit: Math is the American word for mathematics, and a sum is some of it.

entries.clue: Greek clothes dressing Greek character, old, old actor (5,5)

indicatorNotes.dressing: the letter goes inside, between the Greek and the clothes, like a dressing between layers

blocks.note: Gr. is the abbreviation for Greek
eta, the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: Traditional Greek costume worn by an elderly Greek performer.
annotation.walkthrough: Old appears twice: the first gives O, the second belongs to the definition. Garbo, the Swedish star of 1920s and 30s Hollywood, is long dead.
annotation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Hollywood film actress of the 1920s and 1930s.
